subject: 00BF08BD4956E5654A7316968B4444DD
introduction: Quddús, the last and foremost of the Báb’s first eighteen disciples, was a young cleric from Bárfurúsh who accompanied the Báb on pilgrimage, led the defenders of Shaykh Ṭabarsí, and was killed in his home town in 1849 at about twenty-seven. These few readings remember him through Bahá’u’lláh’s eyes, protected in an attack, walking beside Him under insult, and through stories of how his rank came to be seen: the scholar who sat by the door and was given the highest seat by morning. Jonathan and David, Stephen with “the face of an angel”, and the parable of the lowest room are near to these scenes. Jesus’s appeal to “Ye are gods” bears on the ecstatic language reading 5 reports.
questions: Reading 8 tells how one night’s conversation reversed the seating in a room. What does the story say about how spiritual rank is recognized?
“There is no difference between you and him except that he looked towards you.” What kind of greatness is being described?
How do you read the report that Quddús and others said “I am God”? What does Jesus’s answer in John suggest?

outside.why: Under attack, Bahá’u’lláh clothed Quddús in His own garments and sent him to safety. The soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.
Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
Insulted in the streets of a town whose notables were friends. A man’s foes shall be they of his own household.

Quddús wrote a book that says throughout “I am God”, and others at Badasht spoke likewise. Jesus, accused of blasphemy for less, cited a psalm: is it not written in your law, I said, Ye are gods? How do the readings understand such language, and how did Jesus defend it?
Known everywhere for wisdom and sanctity, and killed young. Of Stephen before the council: they saw his face as it had been the face of an angel.
“There is no difference between you and him except that he looked towards you.” The Baptist: he must increase, but I must decrease.
Quddús took the seat near the door, and by morning the host had given him his own. Go and sit down in the lowest room; that when he that bade thee cometh, he may say unto thee, Friend, go up higher.
He was not then recognized as a man of rank. Man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart.
He attained “the supreme martyrdom”. They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, were slain with the sword: of whom the world was not worthy.

shortfall: Reading 3, 4, 6 and 10 concern meetings, tablets and rank within the Báb’s community for which no companion was sought.
